metadata.technology_specification: Discrete graphics processing unit (GPU) with GDDR6 memory
metadata.technology_reasoning: Discrete GPUs with dedicated GDDR6 memory are the prevailing standard in PC and workstation graphics cards as of 2024, widely adopted for gaming, professional visualization, and AI workloads due to their superior performance and memory bandwidth compared to integrated or older memory types.

components.reasoning: This is the core semiconductor chip responsible for graphics computation, always present as the fundamental processing element in every GPU.
Dedicated high-bandwidth memory is essential for performance in modern discrete GPUs, typically provided as separate memory chips soldered onto the PCB.
The substrate that hosts and interconnects the GPU die, memory, power regulation, and other components, universally present as a distinct assembly.
Provides stable and precise power delivery to the GPU and memory, usually composed of separate power stages and controller ICs grouped as a dedicated power subsystem.
A critical subsystem for thermal management, almost all discrete GPUs include an active cooling assembly that is procured or manufactured separately from the PCB assembly.
The standardized electrical and mechanical interface to the motherboard, integral and always present as part of the PCB assembly.
Many modern GPUs include a metal backplate for rigidity and heat dissipation; while common, it can vary by manufacturer and model.
Stores firmware controlling GPU initialization and settings, typically a separate component soldered on the PCB.
